title: feat(sharing): hierarchy managers may manage shares within their write DEPTH (ADR-0111 D1 DEPTH, framework)
body:
## What this is

The **framework side of ADR-0111's D1 DEPTH extension** — the last open framework piece of ADR-0111. Follows P0 (#3965), P1 (#3975), and D8 framework (#3986), all merged.

P0 shipped `canManageShares` as **owner + Modify All Data**, with DEPTH named as a follow-up. This lands it: a **hierarchy manager** may now manage shares (grant / revoke / list) on a record whose owner falls within their write DEPTH — matching Salesforce (roles above the owner) and Dataverse (the `Share` privilege's BU depth).

## The change

- **`ISecurityService.resolveWriteScope(object, context)`** — the caller's effective write scope (`own` / `own_and_reports` / `unit` / `unit_and_below` / `org`), resolved by the same evaluator (`getEffectiveScope('write', …)`) the CRUD middleware uses. Fails closed to `own`. Mirrored on the sharing plugin's structural `SharingSecurityProbe`.
- **`canManageShares` DEPTH branch** — after the owner and Modify-All checks, if the caller's write scope is a **hierarchy** scope, expand it via the already-bound enterprise `hierarchy-scope-resolver` (`resolveOwnerScopeIds`, the same owner set the write filter / `canEdit` use) and allow when the record's owner is in it.

## The `org` trap, closed by construction

`resolveWriteScope` returns `org` for **two** reasons: a genuine `modifyAllRecords` holder, **and** the fail-OPEN "no permission set mentions this object" default. So the DEPTH branch honours **only** the three hierarchy scopes and deliberately **ignores `org`** — org-wide management stays gated exclusively by the explicit `hasWriteBypass` (Modify All) check from P0. A caller on a fail-open `org` object with no real Modify-All grant is correctly denied. There's a dedicated test for this.

## Fails closed

No security service, or no enterprise resolver (the open edition), → the DEPTH branch is inert and authority stays exactly P0's owner + Modify-All. A throwing probe denies.

## Testing

- New `canManageShares` DEPTH cases in `sharing-service.test.ts`: manager whose `own_and_reports`/`unit` set covers the owner → allowed; a peer whose set does not → denied; **`org` from the probe does NOT widen** (fail-open guard); `own` adds nothing beyond ownership; **manager scope with no resolver → owner-only fallback**.
- Full suites green: plugin-sharing **198**, plugin-security **677**, spec **6886**. Generated-artifact checks (`spec-changes` / `upgrade-guide` / `authorable-surface` / `api-surface` / `skill-docs`) pass; changed files lint clean; packages build.

## Docs

`services.sharing` management-authority section (now lists the hierarchy-manager path), ADR-0111 status + D1 body (DEPTH landed).

## Remaining ADR-0111 scope

With this, **all framework-side ADR-0111 work is done** (P0, P1/D3, D8, D1-DEPTH). What's left is the **cloud** side — batched into one `.objectstack-sha` bump in `objectstack-ai/cloud` picking up P0+P1+D8+D1-DEPTH, plus `security-enterprise` integration tests for the manager-revoke and hierarchy-manager-manage paths, and confirming `HttpDispatcher.handleShareLinks` (no wiring change expected).
